basis: Defined as an inborn glycosylation disorder; no evidence supplied for additional organ damage.
Hereditary mixed polyposis affects the intestinal mucosa; subsequent cancer risk does not add an axis.
Corynebacterial infection of the nasopharynx; myocarditis and neuropathy are minority complications.
Cutaneous neoplasm of T lymphocytes and a lymphoma; marrow, splenic and hepatic involvement are each annotated at 5-29%.
Congenital structural abnormality of the esophagus; aspiration pneumonia is a separately diagnosed complication.
Heme synthesis disorder with defining neurovisceral dysfunction; direct porphyric renal impairment occurs in 30-79%; hepatic synthesis and abdominal pain alone do not establish organ injury.
Defining cerebellar malformation, ataxia and developmental impairment; retinopathy 1/4; isolated optic pallor and hepatomegaly reports do not establish common additional damage.
Repeated scratching produces chronic lichenified skin damage; the name does not establish neurologic disease or an immune mechanism.
Defining rib, scapular, chest wall and mandibular malformations with Pierre Robin sequence and cleft palate; no established additional organ damage.
Organic acid metabolism defect defined by striatal injury and dystonic encephalopathy; feeding and swallowing dysfunction reflect neurologic disease.
Adrenal steroid synthesis deficiency; salt wasting reflects hormonal deficiency rather than intrinsic renal damage, and pigmentation does not establish skin injury.
Immune-mediated targetoid skin disease; erosive oral mucositis occurs in roughly 25-60%, near the threshold; lasting ocular damage is uncommon.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis; cardiomyopathy reported in 1/2 annotated patients; organomegaly alone lacks damage evidence; abnormal visual responses may be central.
Degenerative visceral smooth muscle disease classified as an intestinal disorder; visceral muscle is gastrointestinal rather than skeletal muscle.
Inherited esophageal achalasia; associated arthritis and sicca findings do not establish common direct extraesophageal damage.
Adenomatous neoplasm originating in the colon or rectum.
Defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability and commonly epilepsy; hypotonia alone does not establish primary muscle disease.
Endocrine pancreatic hyperinsulinism; neurodevelopmental impairment is annotated at 30-79%, supporting hypoglycemic brain injury; cardiomyopathy is only 5-29%.
Benign smooth muscle tumor arising in the breast; breast has no axis, and smooth muscle origin does not imply skeletal muscle disease.
Developmental impairment is shared across the major 2p deletion syndromes; renal, metabolic and other structural abnormalities depend on the deleted interval.
Hereditary juvenile open-angle glaucoma damages the ocular optic nerve.
Neurodevelopmental impairment predominates across 9q deletion syndromes; cardiac, skeletal and other anomalies vary by deleted interval without a common frequency established here.
Defining craniofacial dysostosis, ocular lesions and ear defects; encephalocele occurs in 30-79%; VSD and cleft lip also occur in 30-79% but are omitted by the four-axis cap.
Defined by congenital structural heart defects, including ventricular septal defect, tetralogy of Fallot and double outlet right ventricle.
Defined by chronic axonal damage to peripheral sensory and motor nerves; secondary weakness does not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle disease.
